cues.en: So the main question to start with is why do functional programmers use so many strange words?
cues.zh: 那么一开始的主要问题是：为什么函数式程序员要用这么多奇怪的词？

cues.en: catamorphism,
cues.zh: catamorphism，

cues.en: applicative, currying, monoid, and monad, the most scary word of all.
cues.zh: 应用函子、柯里化、幺半群，以及最吓人的词——单子。

cues.en: And I I think the problem is these words kind of sound scary, but they're not actually
cues.zh: 我觉得问题在于，这些词听起来有点吓人，但其实它们并不是

cues.zh: 如果你明白它们是什么，概念并不可怕。我的意思是，你可能像这里的 Homer 一样，觉得自己不可能理解这些东西。这太复杂了。

cues.en: But it's not... I don't think it's scary. I think it's unfamiliar.

cues.zh: 如果你知道这些词是什么意思，或者至少揭开一点神秘面纱，那你可能就会像这里的 Homer 一样说：行吧，你支持映射。如果我叫它“可映射”，或者“可折叠”，我就能理解了，

cues.en: or an aggregatable. Whatever the word is, it doesn't really matter what the words are, but these words don't sound as scary as the sort of mathematical words. So that's really the goal of this talk is to demystify. You may not know what they mean,
cues.zh: 或者叫“可聚合”。不管用什么词，叫什么其实无所谓，但这些词听起来绝不像那些数学术语那么吓人。所以这次演讲的目标就是为大家祛魅。你可能依然不知道它们到底是什么意思，

cues.zh: 光 SOLID 就包含五种东西，还有 IoC、DI、ABC 等等。如果你是个 OO 老手，可能根本意识不到这有多吓人。

cues.en: words.

cues.zh: 所以有个东西，我称之为函数式工具箱，它类似于

cues.zh: 每个工具都擅长做一件特定的事。如果你是个有经验的人，你知道该用哪个工具做哪件事。函数式程序员也有一堆工具，

cues.en: that functional programs need to solve? Well, first problem they need to solve is composition,
cues.zh: 哪些类型的问题呢？首先需要解决的问题是组合，

cues.en: because everything in functional programming is composition. It's the kind of fundamental principle, and I'll talk about it in a second.
cues.zh: 因为函数式编程中的一切都是组合。这是基本原则，我马上会讲到。

cues.en: How do you combine things? How do you aggregate things? That's a common problem in both OO and functional.
cues.zh: 你如何组合东西？你如何聚合东西？这是面向对象和函数式中常见的问题。

cues.en: How do you iterate through things?

cues.zh: 你如何处理副作用？这更偏向函数式编程。

cues.zh: 程序员总是……总是在谈论副作用。那副作用到底指什么？我会解释我们所说的副作用。

cues.zh: 但有时处理这些副作用挺棘手的，所以你得把有副作用和无副作用的东西混合起来，或者把它们串起来，又或者并行处理它们。有副作用时，你需要处理各种不同的情况，

cues.zh: 你会经常看到这些术语。组合使用 compose 关键字。

cues.zh: 在函数式编程中，遍历通常叫作 fold。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 那么

cues.en: start with some principles of statically typed functional programming for people who are newbies.
cues.zh: 先从静态类型函数式编程的一些原则讲起，给新手们。

cues.en: The first thing is that functions are things,
cues.zh: 第一点是函数也是东西，

cues.en: and like to use a little railway track analogy, and the composition is used everywhere. So So there's no inheritance. There's nothing else. It's... Everything is composition. And if you know how to use Lego,
cues.zh: 我喜欢用铁轨的类比，而组合无处不在。所以没有继承。没有别的。就是……一切都是组合。如果你会用乐高，

cues.en: you know how to do composition because it's exactly the same.
cues.zh: 你就会组合，因为完全一样。

cues.en: So let's look at functions as things.
cues.zh: 那我们把函数看作东西。

cues.en: So a function is a little thing. I I like to use the railway track analogy. And there's a little tunnel tunnel transformation,
cues.zh: 函数就是个小东西。我喜欢用铁轨类比。有个小隧道变换，

cues.en: something goes in and something comes out. In this case, an apple goes in and it turns into banana. So this is a... We call this an apple to banana function. Right? It it transforms apples into bananas.
cues.zh: 东西进去，东西出来。这里，苹果进去，变成香蕉。所以这是……我们称之为苹果到香蕉的函数。对吧？它把苹果变成香蕉。

cues.en: And the thing about functions is they are standalone things. They're not attached to any class.
cues.zh: 函数的特点是它们是独立的东西，不依附于任何类。

cues.en: Because they're things, they can be used just like you might use an integer or a string or something. You can pass them around as parameters.
cues.zh: 因为它们是东西，所以可以像使用整数、字符串之类的东西一样使用它们。你可以把它们作为参数传递。

cues.en: You can put them in lists.
cues.zh: 你可以把它们放进列表里。

cues.en: You can do all sorts of things because they're just things just like everything else.
cues.zh: 你可以做各种各样的事情，因为它们就是东西，和其他所有东西一样。

cues.en: And this standalone thing is really, really important because standalone is another word for reusable.
cues.zh: 这种独立性非常重要，因为独立就是可复用的另一种说法。

cues.en: If it's on its own, it can be reused in any context. If it's part of a class, it's really hard to extract it from that class and reuse it in a different context. But all the functions in functional programming are standalone functions.
cues.zh: 如果它是独立的，就可以在任何上下文中复用。如果它是类的一部分，就很难把它从那个类里抽出来，在不同的上下文中复用。而函数式编程中的所有函数都是独立函数。

cues.en: So here's an example
cues.zh: 这里有个例子

cues.en: of a function that has a normal input,
cues.zh: 一个函数，它有普通输入，

cues.en: but it has an output, which is a function.
cues.zh: 但它的输出是一个函数。

cues.en: Here's an example of a function that has a function as an input and a normal output. Here's a function with a normal input and a normal output,
cues.zh: 这里有个例子，一个函数以函数为输入、以普通值为输出。这里有个函数，普通输入、普通输出，

cues.en: but it's got this extra function which can be used as parameterizing
cues.zh: 但它多了这个函数，可以用来参数化

cues.en: it.
cues.zh: 它。

cues.en: And this would be called the strategy pattern in OO.
cues.zh: 在面向对象里，这叫策略模式。

cues.en: So this is... That's it. That's really everything you need know about functional programming right there. If you understand that, you understand everything.
cues.zh: 所以这就是……就这样。关于函数式编程，你真正需要知道的就这些。如果你理解了这个，你就理解了一切。

cues.en: You can see it can get really complex. It's a it's a very simple foundation, but you can have functions that return other functions that generate other functions, which you use as parameters to other function. It can get very complicated, but the fundamental principles
cues.zh: 你可以看到它能变得非常复杂。它的基础非常简单，但你可以有返回其他函数的函数，那些函数又生成其他函数，你再把它们作为参数传给别的函数。它可以变得非常复杂，但基本原理

cues.en: are basically just what I said in the last few minutes.
cues.zh: 基本上就是我刚才几分钟里说的那些。

cues.en: And most of the tools
cues.zh: 大部分工具

cues.en: in the functional toolbox that I'm gonna be talking about
cues.zh: 在我将要讲到的函数式工具箱里

cues.en: are
cues.zh: 都是

cues.en: function transformers.
cues.zh: 函数转换器。

cues.en: They take functions in, and they spit other functions out.
cues.zh: 它们接收函数，再吐出新函数。

cues.en: So having functions come in and functions come out, that's a really, really common thing in functional programming.
cues.zh: 所以函数进、函数出，这在函数式编程里非常非常常见。

cues.en: So the next principle, which is really important, is composition.
cues.zh: 下一个原则非常重要，就是组合。

cues.en: So I'm gonna talk about LEGO for a second because everyone understands how LEGO works, hopefully.
cues.zh: 我稍微聊聊乐高，因为希望大家都懂乐高怎么玩。

cues.en: And LEGO actually has a sort of philosophy, right, which is that everything is designed to be connected to everything else.
cues.zh: 乐高其实有一套哲学，对吧，就是每个零件都设计成能跟其他所有零件相连。

cues.en: Right? You don't have LEGO pieces which don't fit to other LEGO pieces. And if you connect two LEGO pieces together, you get another piece which can still be connected to other pieces.
cues.zh: 对吧？不会有乐高零件装不上别的乐高零件。而且你把两个零件拼在一起，得到的还是一个能继续拼接的零件。

cues.en: You run into a wall where, oh, I can no longer add any more LEGO pieces because I've run out of dots or something. And
cues.zh: 你不会遇到“哎呀，我没法再加乐高零件了，因为凸点用完了”这种墙。而且

cues.en: they're reusable.
cues.zh: 它们可复用。

cues.en: So here's some LEGO. Every single piece in LEGO has little dots, so they're designed to be connected.
cues.zh: 这就是乐高。每个零件上都有小凸点，就是为连接而设计的。

cues.en: And when you start assembling them,
cues.zh: 当你开始拼装时，

cues.en: you can just keep adding and adding pieces.
cues.zh: 你可以一直加、一直加。

cues.en: They're designed to be that way, that you never sort of hit a boundary. You can add two pieces, that makes another piece. You add more pieces.
cues.zh: 它们就是这么设计的，你永远不会撞到什么边界。你拼两块，就成了另一块。你再继续加。

cues.en: You don't need a special adapter. You don't say, well, this piece won't fit with this piece because then need a special sort of adapter pattern to make two bits of Lego fit. No. You don't have an adapter pattern in LEGO. They just literally
cues.zh: 你不需要专门的适配器。你不用说什么“这块装不上那块，得来个特殊的适配器模式才能让两块乐高拼上”。不。乐高里没有适配器模式。它们就是字面意义上

cues.en: connect straight together.
cues.zh: 直接连在一起。

cues.en: And you can keep adding and adding and adding.
cues.zh: 而且你可以不断添加、不断添加。

cues.en: And you can make really, really big things out of LEGO, out of all the small pieces.
cues.zh: 你可以用乐高做出非常非常大的东西，用那些小零件。

cues.en: And here's the reusability thing. Right? You can you can make something, and then you can disassemble it and make something else. The pieces themselves,
cues.zh: 这就是可复用性。对吧？你可以做出某个东西，然后拆开它，再做别的东西。零件本身

cues.en: do not have any strings attached. Literally, they don't have any strings attached. If they had strings attached, they'll get tangled up. The strings will get tangled up.
cues.zh: 没有任何附加束缚。真的，它们没有任何绳子绑着。如果有绳子绑着，就会缠在一起。绳子会缠在一起。

cues.en: And this is one of the goals of functional programming is that all the functions that you build don't have any strings attached. And because of that, they're reusable. They're not attached to a particular context.
cues.zh: 这就是函数式编程的目标之一：你构建的所有函数都没有任何附加束缚。正因如此，它们可复用。它们不依附于特定上下文。

cues.en: You don't have to extract them in order to reuse them. They literally are designed to be reusable from the very beginning.
cues.zh: 你不必为了复用而把它们抽出来。它们从一开始就是为可复用而设计的。

cues.en: So you can make really big things
cues.zh: 所以你可以做出非常大的东西

cues.en: from small things in LEGO.
cues.zh: 用乐高的小零件。

cues.en: That's what I like to call the power of composition.
cues.zh: 这就是我喜欢称之为组合的力量。

cues.en: Now let's look at the functional programming philosophy, which is very similar to the Lego philosophy.
cues.zh: 现在我们来看看函数式编程哲学，它和乐高哲学非常相似。

cues.en: And this is, by the way, I'm talking about statically typed functional programming.
cues.zh: 顺便说一下，我说的是静态类型的函数式编程。

cues.en: The dynamically typed dynamic functional programming is similar, but there's a little bit of difference. So in functional programming, you try to design functions that do one thing well, the SOLID principles applied to functional programming too.
cues.zh: 动态类型的函数式编程类似，但有一些差别。在函数式编程中，你尽量设计只做好一件事的函数，SOLID 原则同样适用于函数式编程。

cues.en: But the functions can be reused. So you design your functions to be reusable,
cues.zh: 但函数是可以复用的。所以你要把函数设计成可复用的，

cues.en: and you design them to work together.
cues.zh: 并且让它们能协同工作。

cues.en: And you expect the output of a function might be the input to some other function.
cues.zh: 你期望一个函数的输出可能是另一个函数的输入。

cues.en: You design them so that you might be working with pieces that you don't even know about yet.
cues.zh: 你设计它们时，要考虑你可能会用到自己都还不知道的组件。

cues.en: And by the way, if you're familiar with the Unix philosophy, this is exactly the same as the Unix
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你熟悉 Unix 哲学，这跟 Unix

cues.en: utility philosophy.
cues.zh: 工具哲学是完全一样的。

cues.en: And in statically typed function
cues.zh: 而在静态类型的函数式

cues.en: programming,
cues.zh: 编程中，

cues.en: we use the types to ensure that the inputs match the outputs. We make sure that you can't accidentally put the wrong kind of thing together.
cues.zh: 我们用类型来确保输入与输出匹配。我们确保你不会不小心把错误类型的东西拼在一起。

cues.en: So this is the functional tool, designing things that do one thing well. The toolkit is a very generic set of functions that you use
cues.zh: 所以这就是函数式工具，设计只做好一件事的东西。工具箱是一组非常通用的函数，你拿它们

cues.en: as your kind of building blocks.
cues.zh: 当作你的构建块。

cues.en: So let's look at function composition.
cues.zh: 那我们来看看函数组合。

cues.en: Here's an apple to banana function, and here's a banana to cherry function.
cues.zh: 这里有一个苹果到香蕉的函数，还有一个香蕉到樱桃的函数。

cues.en: And how would you glue them together? How do you compose them? How do you make... How do you connect them? Well, it's really obvious if they're railway track. You just literally stick the two pieces together, and you get a new function.
cues.zh: 你怎么把它们粘在一起？怎么组合它们？怎么……怎么连接它们？其实如果它们是铁轨就一目了然了。你 literally 把两块拼在一起，就得到一个新函数。

cues.en: And what's cool about this is that you can't tell that this was built from smaller functions.
cues.zh: 这酷的地方在于，你根本看不出它是由更小的函数构建的。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: you now have another function that you can then use to build a bigger function and so on and so forth. And also what's cool is the banana has disappeared.
cues.zh: 你现在有了另一个函数，可以用来构建更大的函数，以此类推。还有一点很酷：香蕉消失了。

cues.en: Where did the banana go?
cues.zh: 香蕉去哪了？

cues.en: You've now got some data hiding. You've got some abstraction.
cues.zh: 你现在有了一些数据隐藏，有了一些抽象。

cues.en: The fact that the thing was built from small pieces, which use something, the bigger function can hide all that. So you've got this nice API.
cues.zh: 这个东西是由小块构建的，它们使用了某些东西，而更大的函数可以把这些都隐藏起来。所以你就有了一个漂亮的 API。

cues.en: And you can build really big things
cues.zh: 你可以构建真正庞大的东西

cues.en: just using functions without any classes or objects or anything. So if you think about a
cues.zh: 只用函数，不需要任何类、对象或其他东西。所以如果你想想一个

cues.en: website,
cues.zh: 网站，

cues.en: a website is a function. An HTTP request comes in, and it spits out an HTTP response. The whole thing is a giant function. It's with an input and output.
cues.zh: 网站就是一个函数。一个 HTTP 请求进来，它吐出一个 HTTP 响应。整个东西就是一个巨大的函数，有输入和输出。

cues.en: And when you do a functional
cues.zh: 当你做函数式

cues.en: design,
cues.zh: 设计时，

cues.en: inside
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: your your main web function,
cues.zh: 你的主 Web 函数内部，

cues.en: you have all these little little functions that do all the little work, and they're all connected together by pipes.
cues.zh: 你有所有这些小函数来做各种小工作，它们都通过管道连接在一起。

cues.en: You don't need classes. You can you seriously build quite sophisticated applications using purely functions.
cues.zh: 你不需要类。你完全可以只用纯函数构建相当复杂的应用。

cues.en: And if you want to call these microservices,
cues.zh: 如果你想调用这些微服务，

cues.en: be my guest.
cues.zh: 请便。

cues.en: Microservices are very similar.
cues.zh: 微服务非常相似。

cues.en: That's another example of a parallel composition.
cues.zh: 那是并行组合的另一个例子。

cues.en: So I have a whole talk on this, if you're interested,
cues.zh: 关于这个我有一整个演讲，如果你感兴趣的话，

cues.en: on my website.
cues.zh: 在我的网站上。

cues.en: Right. So let's look at number one tool.
cues.zh: 好，那我们来看看第一个工具。

cues.en: Number one tool is monoids.
cues.zh: 第一个工具是幺半群。

cues.en: Okay?
cues.zh: 好吗？

cues.en: Or tool number one. That's not not the number one tool. It's the first tool that I'm gonna be talking.
cues.zh: 或者说工具一号。那不是头号工具，而是我要讲的第一个工具。

cues.en: And there's gonna be some mathematics here, so I hope this won't put you off. Okay? If you... If you're scared of mathematics, then let's see. So this is the first piece of mathematics,
cues.zh: 这里会有一些数学，希望这不会吓到你。好吗？如果你……如果你怕数学，那咱们看看。这是第一段数学，

cues.en: and this is the second piece of mathematics,
cues.zh: 这是第二段数学，

cues.en: and this is the third piece of mathematics.
cues.zh: 这是第三段数学。

cues.en: So this is all the mathematics I'm gonna use. So if you can understand this, you were right.
cues.zh: 这就是我要用到的全部数学。所以如果你能理解这些，你就说对了。

cues.en: So what's interesting is that mathematicians are a little bit like programmers, and they always like to make things abstract. They're always looking for patterns. So a mathematician would look at this and say, well, this is interesting.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，数学家有点像程序员，他们总喜欢把东西抽象化。他们总是在寻找模式。所以数学家看到这个会说，嗯，这挺有意思。

cues.en: I can see a pattern. I can see some patterns here.
cues.zh: 我能看出一个模式。我能看出这里有些模式。

cues.en: And let's look at this pattern. We've got some things,
cues.zh: 来看看这个模式。我们有一些东西，

cues.en: and we've got some way of combining them.
cues.zh: 并且我们有一种组合它们的方式。

cues.en: And the result is another of the same kind of thing. You add two integers, you get another integer back.
cues.zh: 结果还是同一种东西。两个整数相加，得到的还是整数。

cues.en: I wonder if that works for anything else.
cues.zh: 我想知道这对其他东西也成立吗。

cues.en: Oh, yeah. It works for multiplication too. If I add... If I multiply two things, I get another thing back, another integer back.
cues.zh: 哦，对。乘法也成立。如果我把……如果我把两个东西相乘，得到的还是另一个东西，另一个整数。

cues.en: What else does it work for? Well, it works for strings. If I have two strings and I concatenate them, I get another string back.
cues.zh: 对其他什么还成立？嗯，对字符串也成立。如果有两个字符串，把它们拼接起来，得到的还是字符串。

cues.en: And if I have two lists and I concatenate them,
cues.zh: 如果有两个列表，把它们拼接起来，

cues.en: I get another list back.
cues.zh: 得到的还是列表。

cues.en: So this is actually quite a common pattern. It happens all over all over the place. Okay.
cues.zh: 所以这其实是个很常见的模式。它到处都在出现。好。

cues.en: What's interesting about this pattern is because when you add two things together,
cues.zh: 这个模式有意思的地方在于，当你把两个东西加在一起，

cues.en: in this case, you add two integers, you get another integer, you can keep going.
cues.zh: 这里是把两个整数相加，得到另一个整数，你可以继续下去。

cues.en: So I can add three to that, and that gives me back another integer.
cues.zh: 所以我可以再给它加三，又得到另一个整数。

cues.en: Right? And so I can add four to that. So I can keep adding and adding and adding just like the Lego. So the Lego analogy is quite good.
cues.zh: 对吧？然后我可以再给它加四。所以我可以一直加、一直加，就像乐高一样。所以乐高的类比挺贴切的。

cues.en: So what we've got, we started off with a pairwise operation,
cues.zh: 我们从两两之间的运算开始，

cues.en: like addition or multiplication
cues.zh: 比如加法或乘法

cues.en: or adding strings together, and we now have
cues.zh: 或者字符串拼接，而现在我们有了

cues.en: an operation that works on lists. We can actually extend it infinitely, adding more and more things without ever running out.
cues.zh: 一个能作用于列表的运算。我们实际上可以无限扩展它，不断增加元素也永远不会耗尽。

cues.en: Anyway, what about the next one?
cues.zh: 总之，接下来看下一个？

cues.en: Is one plus two plus three is the same as one plus two plus three.
cues.zh: 一加二加三和一加二加三是一样的。

cues.en: What that means is that the order of
cues.zh: 这意味着

cues.en: combining the things doesn't matter. If you combine two plus three first or you combine one plus two first, it doesn't make any difference.
cues.zh: 合并元素的顺序无关紧要。无论是先算二加三，还是先算一加二，都没有区别。

cues.en: So you could do one plus two, and then you could add three, then you could add four, or you could do one plus two here, and three plus four here, and then add them later on. It really doesn't matter which way you do it. You always get the same answer.
cues.zh: 所以你可以先算一加二，再加三，再加四；或者这里算一加二，那里算三加四，然后再加起来。怎么做都完全无所谓，答案总是一样的。

cues.en: So that's good. Now it's not always true. Like subtraction, it doesn't work with.
cues.zh: 这很好。但它并不总是成立。比如减法就不适用。

cues.en: The order does matter for subtraction. So subtraction doesn't fit this pattern.
cues.zh: 对减法来说顺序确实重要。所以减法不符合这个模式。

cues.en: Okay. What about this zero thing?
cues.zh: 好。那这个零是怎么回事？

cues.en: What
cues.zh: 这个

cues.en: does this zero mean? So a mathematician would say, well, this is very interesting. We have this very special kind of thing that when you use it to combine... You combine it with this other thing, you always get back the original thing. Like, zero leaves it alone. It it kind of doesn't do anything.
cues.zh: 零是什么意思？数学家会说，这很有意思。我们有这样一种非常特殊的东西，当你用它来结合……把它和另一个东西结合时，你总是得到原来的那个东西。就像零不改变它一样，它基本上什么也不做。

cues.en: It's it's a kind of a null pattern.
cues.zh: 这是一种空值模式。

cues.en: And it turns out that zero is quite a common thing. So when you have multiplication,
cues.zh: 事实证明，“零”其实是一个很普遍的概念。比如在乘法中，

cues.en: there's a special thing that when you multiply,
cues.zh: 有这么一个特殊的数，任何数乘上它，

cues.en: you get the same thing back, and that would be the number one.
cues.zh: 结果都还是原来的数，那就是数字 1。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: if you have strings,
cues.zh: 如果是字符串，

cues.en: there's a special thing that when you add it to any other string, you get the same string back, and that's the empty string,
cues.zh: 也有个特殊的字符串，把它追加到任何其他字符串上，结果都还是原来的字符串，那就是空字符串，

cues.en: and so on and so forth, the empty list.
cues.zh: 诸如此类，还有空列表。

cues.en: There's a zero, conceptual zero, for all these kinds of things. It's very, very common.
cues.zh: 这类事物都有一个“零”，一个概念上的“零”。这非常非常普遍。

cues.en: Right. So here's here's the pattern that we've recognized. We've got a bunch of things.
cues.zh: 好，这就是我们总结出来的模式。我们有一组元素，

cues.en: We've got some way of combining them two at a time,
cues.zh: 有一套两两结合它们的方法，

cues.en: and that's...
cues.zh: 而且……

cues.en: The first rule we have is the closure rule. When you combine them, you get another thing of the same type.
cues.zh: 第一条规则是闭包规则：结合之后，得到的仍是同类型的元素。

cues.en: And the second rule is associativity,
cues.zh: 第二条规则是结合律，

cues.en: which is when you combine them more than one thing, it doesn't really matter which order you combine them in.
cues.zh: 也就是结合多个元素时，先结合哪几个并不会影响结果。

cues.en: And the third thing is there's a zero or an identity element
cues.zh: 第三条规则是存在一个“零”或单位元，

cues.en: that when you combine it with a thing, you get the same thing back. So it doesn't
cues.zh: 它与任何元素结合，结果都保持不变。所以它并没有

cues.en: do anything.
cues.zh: 起任何作用。

cues.en: These patterns are pretty obvious
cues.zh: 稍微想想就会发现，

cues.en: patterns if you start thinking about it, and the mathematicians have a word for this thing. They call it a monoid. So here's the mathematical jargon for something,
cues.zh: 这些模式显而易见，数学家对它有个专门的称谓，叫做“幺半群”（monoid）。所以这就是个数学黑话，

cues.en: which if you if you just look at it from pattern analysis,
cues.zh: 但如果你纯粹从模式分析的角度来看，

cues.en: it's like, yeah, this is kind of quite a common pattern that I would recognize.
cues.zh: 就会觉得：没错，这确实是一种很常见、很容易识别出的模式。

cues.en: So let's stop with the jargon. Homer says, no more jargon. Don't talk about monoids. Why is doing... Analyzing
cues.zh: 所以咱们别再堆术语了。Homer 说，不要再讲术语了。别谈幺半群。为什么做……分析

cues.en: these patterns, why is it useful? How
cues.zh: 这些模式，为什么有用？它

cues.en: is it useful as a programmer?
cues.zh: 对程序员来说有什么用？

cues.en: Well, if you think about the closure rule, the fact that you can combine two things and get another thing, that means that all pairwise operations can be converted into things that work on lists.
cues.zh: 想想闭包规则，你能把两个东西组合起来得到另一个东西，这意味着所有成对运算都能转换成作用于列表的运算。

cues.en: So we just start with a pair, and you add up the list.
cues.zh: 所以我们从一对开始，然后累加到列表上。

cues.en: And this is normally called reduce.
cues.zh: 这通常叫做 reduce。

cues.en: So if you have one plus two plus three plus four,
cues.zh: 所以如果你有 1+2+3+4，

cues.en: you have the plus pairwise operation,
cues.zh: 你有加法这个成对运算，

cues.en: and you can take a list of integers, one two three four, and reduce it using plus.
cues.zh: 你可以拿一个整数列表，1 2 3 4，用加法来 reduce 它。

cues.en: So the reduce operation, all it does is basically take the list of items and stick that pairwise operation in between every single one.
cues.zh: 所以 reduce 操作，它做的就是拿一个元素列表，把那个成对运算塞进每两个元素之间。

cues.en: You have multiplicate...
cues.zh: 你有乘法……

cues.en: Reduce is a very common practice, one of the things in our function toolbox.
cues.zh: Reduce 是非常常见的做法，是我们函数工具箱里的工具之一。

cues.en: If you have multiplication,
cues.zh: 如果你有乘法，

cues.en: that's the pairwise operation. We can then take a list of numbers, we can reduce it using multiplication.
cues.zh: 那就是成对运算。我们可以拿一个数字列表，用乘法来 reduce 它。

cues.en: Right? And we can take a list of strings, do the same thing. Rather than adding them up pairwise, we can collapse an entire
cues.zh: 对吧？我们也可以拿一个字符串列表，做同样的事。不是成对相加，而是把整个

cues.en: list of strings into a single string using the string concatenation operator and so on and so forth for lists.
cues.zh: 字符串列表用字符串拼接运算符折叠成一个字符串，列表上也是类似的道理。

cues.en: So this is a really, really common pattern.
cues.zh: 所以这是一个非常非常常见的模式。

cues.en: Now the associativity,
cues.zh: 然后是结合律，

cues.en: the benefit of associativity,
cues.zh: 结合律的好处，

cues.en: there's all sorts of things. Divide and conquer, the parallelization,
cues.zh: 有各种各样的好处。分治法、并行化、

cues.en: incremental accumulation. I'll talk about parallelization right now. So parallelization
cues.zh: 增量累积。我现在就讲讲并行化。并行化

cues.en: means that you can take a bunch of stuff and you can spread it out over multiple CPUs or multiple machines or whatever. So let's say we have to add up one and two and three and four.
cues.zh: 意味着你可以拿一堆东西，把它们分散到多个 CPU 或多台机器等等上面。假设我们要把 1、2、3、4 加起来。

cues.en: We could parallelize it and say we'll do one plus two on this machine, and we'll do three plus four on this machine. Then we'll take the results, and we'll add them together.
cues.zh: 我们可以把它并行化，说我们在这台机器上算一加二，在那台机器上算三加四。然后取结果，把它们加起来。

cues.en: Now, obviously,
cues.zh: 显然，

cues.en: you wouldn't do that with four numbers. It's ridiculous. But if you have a million or 10,000,000 things to do,
cues.zh: 你不会拿四个数字这么干。太荒唐了。但如果你有一百万或一千万件事要做，

cues.en: and pairwise
cues.zh: 而且两两

cues.en: operations are quite complicated,
cues.zh: 运算相当复杂，

cues.en: then this is great. So if you have a monoid, you you can instantly parallelize it.
cues.zh: 那就很棒了。所以如果你有一个幺半群，你就能瞬间并行化。

cues.en: Now it it turns out we don't normally... Most of us don't have to worry about parallelization,
cues.zh: 事实证明我们通常不……我们大多数人不用操心并行化，

cues.en: but another really useful thing is incremental accumulation, which is much more common.
cues.zh: 但另一个非常有用的东西是增量累加，这要常见得多。

cues.en: So let's say that your boss asked you to add up plus two plus three,
cues.zh: 假设你老板让你算一加二加三，

cues.en: because your boss your boss is no good at at mathematics.
cues.zh: 因为你老板数学不怎么样。

cues.en: And she's okay. And then the next day,
cues.zh: 她还算行。然后第二天，

cues.en: your boss says, actually, I've changed my mind. Can you add up one plus two plus three plus four today?
cues.zh: 你老板说，其实我改主意了。你今天能算一加二加三加四吗？

cues.en: And then you say, well, I have to start all over again. You know, I just had it, and now I have to go all the back to the beginning and add up one and two and three. No. You don't. Of course. You can keep the number that you calculated yesterday
cues.zh: 然后你说，那我得从头再来一遍。你知道，我刚算完，现在又得回到开头，把一、二、三加起来。不。你不用。当然。你可以保留昨天算出的数

cues.en: and just add four to it. You don't have to add the whole thing up from the very beginning because of this associativity.
cues.zh: 然后只给它加四。你不必从头把整个加一遍，因为有结合律。

cues.en: I've already calculated one and two and three,
cues.zh: 我已经算好了一加二加三，

cues.en: which is six,
cues.zh: 也就是六，

cues.en: and all I have to do is add four to it. So I don't have to start from scratch. I can incrementally accumulate.
cues.zh: 我只要给它加四就行。所以我不必从零开始。我可以增量累加。

cues.en: So every time you have a monoid, you can incrementally accumulate data.
cues.zh: 每次遇到幺半群，你都可以增量地累积数据。

cues.en: And finally, we have all these issues we run into. How do I reduce when the list is empty? How do I do a divide and conquer when one of the steps is empty? How do I do incremental accumulation
cues.zh: 最后，我们会遇到这些问题。列表为空时怎么归约？某一步为空时怎么做分治？没有起始数据时

cues.en: when I don't have any starting data?
cues.zh: 怎么做增量累积？

cues.en: And that's what the identity element is really good for. It's the initial value
cues.zh: 这正是单位元大显身手的地方。它就是初始值，

cues.en: for empty data or missing data. So you have these three things, and you can and you can... Once you see this pattern, you start seeing it everywhere.
cues.zh: 用于空数据或缺失数据。有了这三样东西，你就能……一旦你看出这个模式，就会到处都看到它。

cues.en: And you can have
cues.zh: 而且你可以有

cues.en: a missing zero. You can have patterns where there's no zero,
cues.zh: 一个缺失的零。你可以有不存在零的模式，

cues.en: and the mathematicians call that a semigroup, which is even more obscure.
cues.zh: 数学家称之为半群，这就更冷门了。

cues.en: So let's look at a real example. Let's say we have to do some aggregation. Let's say we have a bunch of order lines,
cues.zh: 来看一个真实例子。假设我们要做聚合。假设有一堆订单行，

cues.en: and we have to add them up and and find out the total.
cues.zh: 我们要把它们加起来，算出总计。

cues.en: Now we could write a loop and and write a specialized piece of code to add them up.
cues.zh: 我们可以写一个循环，写一段专门的代码把它们加起来。

cues.en: The problem with that, again, is if if I've... Again, with three or four things, it's not a problem. But if I have a million things, then tomorrow I have a million the first thing,
cues.zh: 这样做的问题还是在于，如果我……同样，三四个东西没问题。但如果我有一百万个东西，明天又有一百万个，

cues.en: I have to start... I have to run the whole loop all over again? No. So let's use the monoid idea
cues.zh: 我就得……我得把整个循环再跑一遍？不。所以让我们用幺半群的思想

cues.en: because that gives us best of all all all possibilities.
cues.zh: 因为它能带给我们所有可能性中的最优解。

cues.en: So rather than trying to write a loop, what I'm gonna do is say, well, you know, integers are monoids, floats are monoids, any combination of a monoid is another monoid. So all the line is a monoid.
cues.zh: 所以与其写循环，我要做的是说，整数是幺半群，浮点数是幺半群，幺半群的任何组合还是幺半群。所以所有订单行构成一个幺半群。

cues.en: And all I have to do is write a pairwise
cues.zh: 我要做的只是写一个两两

cues.en: combiner
cues.zh: 组合器

cues.en: where I just add the two pieces and return the new thing. I have a pairwise combiner, which is normally pretty straightforward to write.
cues.zh: 也就是把两部分相加并返回新东西。我有一个两两组合器，通常写起来很直接。

cues.en: And then once I've got the pairwise combiner,
cues.zh: 然后一旦有了这个两两组合器，

cues.en: I can run it on the entire list. Just reduce the entire list using the pairwise combiner.
cues.zh: 我就能把它跑在整个列表上。就是用这个两两组合器归约整个列表。

cues.en: So there you go. There's
cues.zh: 所以就是这样。这里有一个

cues.en: a pattern that would be useful. And like I say, if I have another order line come in tomorrow,
cues.zh: 会很有用的模式。而且就像我说的，如果明天又来一条订单行，

cues.en: I don't have to
cues.zh: 我不必

cues.en: recalculate
cues.zh: 重新计算

cues.en: the entire total from scratch.
cues.zh: 整个总额，从头算起。

cues.en: I can just add this extra one by using the incremental accumulation principle.
cues.zh: 我可以用增量累积原则，把这一条额外加上。

cues.en: Profit.
cues.zh: 赚到了。

cues.en: Now a lot of situations, you don't have monoids.
cues.zh: 很多情况下，你并没有幺半群。

cues.en: So for example, I have a bunch of customers,
cues.zh: 比如，我有一堆客户，

cues.en: and I wanna find out how... Let's say I keep track of how many times they visit my website and how much money they spend or whatever. I'd like to add all that stuff up, but I can't because customers are not monoids.
cues.zh: 我想弄清楚……比如说，我记录他们访问我网站多少次、花了多少钱之类的。我想把所有这些都加起来，但做不到，因为客户不是幺半群。

cues.en: However,
cues.zh: 不过，

cues.en: I could create a special kind of class or a structure called customer statistics,
cues.zh: 我可以创建一种特殊的类或结构，叫 customer statistics，

cues.en: which is just integers and stuff, and that would be a monoid because it's all kind of numbers.
cues.zh: 里面就是整数之类的东西，而它会是幺半群，因为全都是数字。

cues.en: So what they typically do
cues.zh: 所以通常的做法是

cues.en: is you take something which isn't a monoid, and you turn it into something which is a monoid.
cues.zh: 拿一个不是幺半群的东西，把它变成幺半群。

cues.en: And once you've got it as a monoid,
cues.zh: 一旦把它变成幺半群，

cues.en: you can then reduce it down. So turning something which isn't in a monoid into a monoid that's MAC and then collapsing the whole thing down into a single value is reduce.
cues.zh: 你就可以把它归约下去。所以，把不是幺半群的东西变成幺半群——也就是 MAC——再把整个东西折叠成单个值，这就是 reduce。

cues.en: And you've probably heard of MapReduce, the MapReduce algorithm.
cues.zh: 你可能听说过 MapReduce，也就是 MapReduce 算法。

cues.en: So that's why it's called MapReduce. It's something to do with monoids.
cues.zh: 这就是它叫 MapReduce 的原因，跟幺半群有点关系。

cues.en: So here is a a nice tweet I saw a long long time ago. Hadoop make me a sandwich. So Hadoop is a is a just... You know, it does parallel computation.
cues.zh: 很久以前我看到过一条有趣的推文：Hadoop 帮我做个三明治。Hadoop 就是……你知道的，它做并行计算。

cues.en: And you start off with... Let's say you start off with some bread and some lettuce and whatever and onion or whatever, you can't just mush them together and make a sandwich. Right? They're not they're not composable.
cues.zh: 你一开始有……比方说有些面包、生菜，还有洋葱之类的，你不能把它们糊在一起就做成三明治，对吧？它们是不可组合的。

cues.en: They're not monoids.
cues.zh: 它们不是幺半群。

cues.en: But if I slice the loaf and I slice the onion and I slice the lettuce,
cues.zh: 但如果我把面包切片、把洋葱切片、把生菜切片，

cues.en: the the slices can be composed of sandwiches.
cues.zh: 这些切片就能组合成三明治。

cues.en: So, you know, you can then reduce the the slices into a into a section of sandwiches.
cues.zh: 于是你就能把这些切片归约成一份份三明治。

cues.en: So this is mapping followed by reduce as a way of, you know, making sandwiches. So it's kind of fun.
cues.zh: 所以这就是先映射再归约，用来做三明治，挺有意思的。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 对。

cues.en: Here's the problem with monoids
cues.zh: 幺半群的问题在于

cues.en: is once you recognize this pattern, you start seeing it everywhere.
cues.zh: 一旦你认出这个模式，就会到处都看到它。

cues.en: For example, if you do DevOps or something and you need to keep track of metrics,
cues.zh: 比如你做 DevOps 之类的工作，需要跟踪指标，

cues.en: there's a little rule saying use counters rather than rates.
cues.zh: 有条小规则说：用计数器，别用速率。

cues.en: And if you say... If you're into monoids, you say, just make sure your metrics are monoids
cues.zh: 如果你……如果你迷上了幺半群，你就会说：只要确保你的指标是幺半群就行

cues.en: because you can do incremental updates and you can handle missing data and so on and so forth.
cues.zh: 因为这样你能做增量更新，还能处理缺失数据等等。

cues.en: And in fact, many, many design patterns are actually monoids behind the scenes. Mark Seaman
cues.zh: 事实上，很多很多设计模式背后其实都是幺半群。Mark Seaman

cues.en: just wrote a blog post the other day about this.
cues.zh: 前几天刚写了一篇关于这个的博客文章。

cues.en: Things like the composite pattern is a monoid. The null object pattern is a monoid.
cues.zh: 组合模式这类东西就是幺半群。空对象模式也是幺半群。

cues.en: Composing commands together to make a new command is a monoid.
cues.zh: 把命令组合起来生成新命令，这也是一种幺半群。

cues.en: And if you're into DDD,
cues.zh: 如果你熟悉 DDD，

cues.en: in the DDD book, they talk about closure of operations.
cues.zh: 《DDD》书里讲到了操作闭包。

cues.en: That's the monoid. So you really start...
cues.zh: 那就是幺半群。所以你真的会开始……

cues.en: You know, it really kind of ruins you, actually.
cues.zh: 你知道，实际上它真的有点把人带偏了。

cues.en: Now you say, why use the word monoid?
cues.zh: 现在你会问，为什么要用“幺半群”这个词？

cues.en: It's a jargony word. But just like any piece of jargon,
cues.zh: 它是个行话词。但就像任何行话一样，

cues.en: once you know what it means, it's a it's a shortcut
cues.zh: 一旦你知道它是什么意思，它就是一个……一个捷径

cues.en: to explaining something quite complicated.
cues.zh: 用来解释相当复杂的东西。

cues.en: So if I say to somebody else and I say, this is a monoid,
cues.zh: 所以如果我对别人说，这是一个幺半群，

cues.en: and they know what that means, assuming they know what that means, they will instantly know
cues.zh: 而他们知道那是什么意思——假设他们知道——他们立刻就会知道

cues.en: that they can parallelize it, that they can do incremental stuff, that it has a zero element, you know, all these kinds of things.
cues.zh: 他们可以把它并行化，可以做增量处理，它有零元素，你知道，诸如此类。

cues.en: So it's a great shortcut for explaining
cues.zh: 所以它是解释……的一个很好的捷径

cues.en: complicated... And they also know what patterns to use, how to work with them straight away.
cues.zh: 复杂的东西……而且他们也知道该用什么模式，知道马上怎么处理它们。

cues.en: What about functional composition? Is that a monoid?
cues.zh: 那函数组合呢？它是幺半群吗？

cues.en: So here's an app... You know, here's our two functions, and we compose them together, and we make this apple to cherry function.
cues.zh: 举个例子……你知道，我们有两个函数，把它们组合起来，就得到了这个“苹果变樱桃”的函数。

cues.en: It's not the same kind of thing. The apple... You know, one thing is an apple to banana function, the other is an apple to cherry function.
cues.zh: 这不是同一类东西。苹果……你知道，一个是“苹果变香蕉”的函数，另一个是“苹果变樱桃”的函数。

cues.en: So composing functions of it is not really a monoid, unfortunately.
cues.zh: 所以不幸的是，这样组合函数并不真的是幺半群。

cues.en: But if we have functions that turn apples into apples
cues.zh: 但如果我们有一些把苹果变成苹果的函数

cues.en: and we combine them, we get another function which turns apples into apples,
cues.zh: 把它们组合起来，就得到另一个把苹果变成苹果的函数，

cues.en: and that is a monoid because it's exactly... The the input functions and the output functions are the same kind of thing. So if you're working with functions that turn integers into integers or strings into strings,
cues.zh: 那就是幺半群，因为正好……输入函数和输出函数是同一类东西。所以如果你处理的是把整数变成整数、或把字符串变成字符串的函数，

cues.en: that... Those kinds of things, you can actually
cues.zh: 那……这类东西，你其实可以

cues.en: do them incrementally. You can do them whatever,
cues.zh: 对它们做增量处理。你可以随便怎么处理，

cues.en: all that kind of stuff because they're monoids.
cues.zh: 诸如此类，因为它们是幺半群。

cues.en: So that's everything you need know about monoids. A set of values, a combining function,
cues.zh: 这就是你需要了解的关于幺半群的全部内容。一组值，一个组合函数，

cues.en: it has all sorts of different words. This is why it says it's a pattern that can recognize because the actual word that you use for the combining function could be anything. So for strings or lists, it's it's normally called concat.
cues.zh: 它有一堆不同的叫法。这就是为什么说它是一个你能认出来的模式，因为组合函数实际叫什么都可以。对于字符串或列表，它通常叫 concat。

cues.en: For integers, it's called plus.
cues.zh: 对于整数，它叫 plus。

cues.en: In Haskell, it's the angle bracket sometimes, and sometimes you see a little plus. All sorts of weird symbols and things, but it's the same concepts everywhere.
cues.zh: 在 Haskell 里，有时是尖括号，有时你会看到一个小加号。各种奇怪的符号和写法都有，但到处都是一样的概念。

cues.en: And this combination, the combiner has to be close associated with zero value.
cues.zh: 而这个组合函数必须封闭、满足结合律，并有一个零值。

cues.en: So here you go. You can use it for reducing a list. You can use it to do parallel computation.
cues.zh: 所以就是这样。你可以用它来归约列表，也可以用它做并行计算。

cues.en: You can use it for doing incremental calculations, all this stuff.
cues.zh: 你可以用它做增量计算，诸如此类。

cues.en: So there you go. That's a monoid.
cues.zh: 就是这样。这就是幺半群。

cues.en: So that's tool number one. Hopefully, monoids are not quite as scary now.
cues.zh: 这是第一件工具。希望现在幺半群没那么吓人了。

cues.en: Right? It's demystified a little bit, I hope.
cues.zh: 对吧？我希望它稍微没那么神秘了。

cues.en: And now we're gonna go even more scary. We're gonna talk about effects.
cues.zh: 接下来我们要讲更吓人的东西。我们要谈效应。

cues.en: So what is an effect? Functional programmers talk about effects all the time.
cues.zh: 那什么是效应？函数式程序员整天都在谈效应。

cues.en: So effect is really just a generic type,
cues.zh: 效应其实就是一个泛型类型，

cues.en: like a list, a list of something.
cues.zh: 比如列表，某个东西的列表。

cues.en: Or it could be a type with some extra data in it, like an option type or a result type.
cues.zh: 或者它可以是带有一些额外数据的类型，比如 option 类型或 result 类型。

cues.en: It could be a type that changes the state of the world, like an async,
cues.zh: 它可以是改变世界状态的类型，比如 async，

cues.en: or it interacts with the world, a task, random number generators,
cues.zh: 或者与世界交互的类型，比如 task、随机数生成器，

cues.en: or it could carry state around like a state type or a causal type. It could be all sorts of things. It's actually kind of vague what an effect is.
cues.zh: 或者它可以携带状态，比如 state 类型或 causal 类型。它可以是各种东西。效应到底是什么，其实有点模糊。

cues.en: It really could be all sorts of stuff. It's basically
cues.zh: 它可能是各种各样的东西。基本上就是

cues.en: really just a generic type that has some...
cues.zh: 一个带有一些……的通用类型。

cues.en: Generic type is a normal type with some extra stuff.
cues.zh: 通用类型就是带有一些额外内容的普通类型。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: I'm going focus on three
cues.zh: 这次演讲我会重点讲三种

cues.en: types in this talk to use them as examples, list, an option, and async.
cues.zh: 类型，用它们举例：列表、Option 和 async。

cues.en: So hopefully everyone knows what list is. The option type, if you're using Java, there's
cues.zh: 希望大家都知道列表是什么。至于 Option 类型，如果你用 Java，

cues.en: an optional stuff built in. Hopefully, most people are familiar with the optional type of some kind.
cues.zh: 里面内置了 Optional。希望大多数人都熟悉某种 Optional 类型。

cues.en: And the async type is... You can think of it as like the task type. It's kind of similar. F uses async and then c uses task.
cues.zh: async 类型……你可以把它看作 Task 类型。两者有点像。F# 用 async，C# 用 Task。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: this whole thing of effects, there's like normal world and effects world. Okay? So in normal world, you have strings, you have integers, you have booleans,
cues.zh: 说到这一整套副作用，有一个普通世界和一个副作用世界。好吧？在普通世界里，有字符串、整数、布尔值，

cues.en: and you have functions
cues.zh: 还有函数

cues.en: that turn strings into... Ints into strings. You have functions that turn int into bools. So this is like your normal world of the normal everyday objects.
cues.zh: 可以把字符串转换成……把整数转换成字符串。也有函数可以把整数转换成布尔值。这就是普通世界，也就是日常对象所在的世界。

cues.en: Now what's interesting is for every kind of effect type, like options and lists and all that, there's a parallel world.
cues.zh: 有意思的是，对于每种副作用类型，比如 Option、列表之类的，都有一个平行世界。

cues.en: It's like a mirror world,
cues.zh: 就像一个镜像世界，

cues.en: and everything in this world is options, for example. So instead of having strings, you have optional strings. Instead of ints, you have optional ints and optional bools.
cues.zh: 这个世界里的所有东西都是 Option。比如，不再是字符串，而是可选字符串；不再是整数，而是可选整数和可选布尔值。

cues.en: And every function that turns an int into a string,
cues.zh: 每个把整数转换成字符串的函数，

cues.en: in optional worlds,
cues.zh: 在 Option 世界里，

cues.en: that function turns optional ints into optional strings,
cues.zh: 都会把可选整数转换成可选字符串，

cues.en: or it turns optional ints into optional bools.
cues.zh: 或者把可选整数转换成可选布尔值。

cues.en: Right? So it's like a parallel universe.
cues.zh: 对吧？所以它就像一个平行宇宙。

cues.en: And same thing with list worlds. In list worlds, everything is lists of things. There's a list of strings and lists of ints and lists of booleans,
cues.zh: 列表世界也是一样。在列表世界里，一切都是事物的列表。有字符串列表、整数列表和布尔值列表，

cues.en: and all the functions turn lists into lists.
cues.zh: 所有函数都把列表变成列表。

cues.en: Well, you know? So
cues.zh: 嗯，你懂的。所以

cues.en: this is my little analogy for these worlds, and it's gonna be quite an important concept. We're gonna be talking about these worlds quite a lot. And async is another world. Everything... You can see how it's going. Right? You can see the pattern here. And so there's this called generic effect. No matter what effect it is, there's some sort of e. I'm gonna call e for generic effect.
cues.zh: 这就是我对这些世界的小类比，这个概念很重要。我们会经常讨论这些世界。异步是另一个世界。一切都……你能看出趋势了。对吧？你能看出这里的模式。所以这叫做泛型效应。不管是什么效应，都有某种 e。我用 e 表示泛型效应。

cues.en: And there's generic
cues.zh: 还有泛型

cues.en: effect types, and there's a a generic effect functions.
cues.zh: 效应类型，以及泛型效应函数。

cues.en: Okay. So that's my effects world.
cues.zh: 好。这就是我的效应世界。

cues.en: So that's the... That's everything you need to know about effects.
cues.zh: 所以这就是……关于效应你需要知道的一切。

cues.en: Just remember, every time you hear someone talk about effects,
cues.zh: 记住，每次听到有人谈论效应，

cues.en: you can probably replace it with option or list or async or whatever.
cues.zh: 你大概都可以把它替换成 option、list、async 或其他什么。

cues.en: So here's here's our first problem is how do we work with these effects? We need to do stuff in the effects world sometimes.
cues.zh: 所以我们的第一个问题是：如何使用这些效应？有时我们需要在效应世界里做事。

cues.en: And how do we do that? And I'll give you some concrete examples.
cues.zh: 怎么做呢？我会给你一些具体例子。

cues.en: So let's say here's the world of normal values, and here's the world of options.
cues.zh: 假设这里是普通值的世界，这里是 option 的世界。

cues.en: And sometimes we have a function
cues.zh: 有时我们有一个函数

cues.en: that takes us from the world... From the normal world into optional world.
